checks.topic: Captured matrix and later time service
checks.result: Same environment.time.renderer_00f8d39c slot supplies the initial captured matrix_1d8 reference and independent later region_84 reads. SystemCameraMatrixService borrows the captured matrix without a second service domain.

The same CameraFrameState and CameraState caches feed matrix and axis writers. Axes use shared projection flag100 and return the timer captured between Y.x load and its store. Time receives that captured pointer directly, reads accumulated with MOVSS, then independently reloads the timer for virtual1C.

Time uses existing camera.projection.fov (native1C4) and full byte174; its returned fog owner is captured before c75.y store. Builder passes that owner plus a reference to the live same camera.fog_184 slot. Fog does not substitute an independent ambient owner.

Builder passes camera.render_mode and exponent word by reference. Lighting preserves captured lighting/first/sentinel across a returning handler, then reads camera mode, environment and sentinel light. Complete and absent scene/lighting/shadow statuses all continue to context and final uploads.

Composed builder does not clear caller-initialized scratch. Optional context uses two actual pointer loads and four raw MOVSS stores only when present; absent scene/shadow still reaches it. Untouched component padding remains the caller preimage.

checks.topic: Final upload captures and COM continuation
checks.result: VS count precedes VS renderer capture; PS reloads both after VS. First failing HRESULT is retained and does not suppress PS; zero count skips guard/device/counters. Capacity and missing-owner failures are explicit host checks.

Stack-local timer, foliage, service matrix, scene/light fields, pointer slots and environment adapters survive the complete synchronous build/upload call. The legacy CRT binding and its referenced preimage words are static; no dangling local runtime binding is published.

The explicit shutdown and the guard declared after the particle access run while callbacks, access, slot and string pool are alive. Domain shutdown clears its published manager, making later guard/domain shutdown calls empty. The slot and callback object outlive the domain.
